confidence_note: Concept; commitment and advancement and the quoted lines are verified across several detailed summaries, not the full text. Old text's invented ten-interview founder, the 'commitment ladder' and 'credit card out' lines dropped.
facts: A meeting counts only if the customer gives up something they value (time, reputation or money) and moves on to the next real step of the sales funnel.
Time: a scheduled next meeting, feedback on wireframes, a trial. Reputation: an introduction to a decision maker or teammate, a public testimonial. Money: letter of intent, pre-order, deposit.
'If you don't know what happens next after a product or sales meeting, the meeting was pointless.'
'The more they're giving up, the more seriously you can take what they're saying.'
Bad endings: 'Looks great, let me know when it launches!' and 'I would definitely buy that.'
Good endings: 'When can we start the trial?' and 'Can I buy the prototype?'
scene_details: a scheduled next meeting with a goal
tension: A meeting full of enthusiasm can still change nothing; the book asks what the other person gave up.
opening_idea: Open on 'Looks great, let me know when it launches!' placed next to 'Can I buy the prototype?'

lessons.idea: Judge a conversation by what the other person gave up and what happens next.
lessons.anchor: time, reputation, money as three kinds of commitment.
lessons.example: A cousin loves your catering idea; the one who books a tasting date has told you more than the one who cheers.

reflect_final: Think of your last meeting about something you are building: what did the other person give up, and what was the next step you both agreed on?

use_cases.situation: A meeting ended warmly with nothing agreed.
use_cases.move: Before you leave, ask for one next step that costs them something: a date for a follow-up with a clear goal.

use_cases.situation: A contact says they love what you are making.
use_cases.move: Ask whether they would introduce you to someone who has the problem; the book counts introductions as reputation.

use_cases.situation: You review your own notes after a customer call.
use_cases.move: Mark each call by what the person gave up and what comes next; if neither is there, mark it as a compliment only.

pocket_idea: A warm meeting with no next step was pointless: ask for time, an introduction or money before you leave.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: If you do not know what happens next after the meeting, the book says the meeting was pointless.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Fitzpatrick's test for a customer meeting is simple: did they give up something they value, and did it move forward? Time, an introduction, a deposit all count. 'Looks great, let me know when it launches' counts for nothing.
